name: ContextMenu

examples.title: Basic ContextMenu
examples.code:
<ContextMenu
  aria-label="Actions for report.pdf"
  trigger={
    <Box tabIndex={0} p="6" textAlign="centered">
      report.pdf: right-click here, or long press on a touch screen
    </Box>
  }
>
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Rename</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Duplicate</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Divider />
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button" color="danger">
    Delete
  </ContextMenu.Item>
</ContextMenu>

examples.title: Nested Regions
examples.code:
<ContextMenu
  aria-label="Board"
  trigger={
    <Box p="5">
      <Paragraph mb="4">Right-click between the cards for the board</Paragraph>
      <ContextMenu
        aria-label="Actions for Write the docs"
        trigger={
          <Card tabIndex={0}>
            <Card.Content>Write the docs</Card.Content>
          </Card>
        }
      >
        <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Move to Done</ContextMenu.Item>
        <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Archive</ContextMenu.Item>
      </ContextMenu>
    </Box>
  }
>
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">New card</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Rename board</ContextMenu.Item>
</ContextMenu>

<ContextMenu
  aria-label="Actions for notes.txt"
  trigger={
    <Box tabIndex={0} p="6" textAlign="centered">
      notes.txt
    </Box>
  }
>
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Open</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Rename</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Divider />
  <ContextMenu.Item as="button">Delete</ContextMenu.Item>
</ContextMenu>

accessibility:
`ContextMenu` follows the [WAI-ARIA menu pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/),
without a menubar or submenus:

- **Opening:** APG names "a command, such as Shift + F10 in Windows, that opens a context specific
  menu". That's the browser's `contextmenu` event, which <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> and the
  context menu key fire on Windows and Linux, and VoiceOver's <kbd>VO</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>M</kbd>
  fires on macOS. `ContextMenu` adds no key handler of its own, so the menu never opens twice for
  one key.
- **Focus on open** goes to the first enabled item, or to the menu itself when there's none.
- <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> move to the next and previous item, wrapping, and
  <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> go to the first and last.
- **Typing** a letter moves to the next item whose text starts with what's been typed. Letters typed
  in quick succession add up to one search, and the same letter again cycles through the items that
  start with it.
- <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> activate the focused item the way a click does, so its
  `onClick` runs, and a key held down activates it once.
- <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes the menu and returns focus to what had it before the menu opened. It
  stops there, so a `Popover` or a `Modal` around the menu stays open.
- <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> close it and return focus too. The menu sits at
  the end of the page, so letting Tab go on from it would skip the rest of the page.
- An item that runs closes the menu and returns focus, unless it moved focus somewhere else, such as
  into a `Modal` it opened or a rename field.

Roles and names:

- The menu is `role="menu"`, named by the `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you pass. There's no
  button to borrow a name from, and a development build warns when a menu opens without one.
- Items are `menuitem` by default, and `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio` with `aria-checked`
  through the item's `role`. A divider is an `<hr>`, which is a separator.
- Disabled items, a `button` with `disabled` or an item with `aria-disabled="true"`, are skipped by
  the arrow keys and by typing, as in `Dropdown`.
- The trigger gets no ARIA, no role and no tab stop. `aria-haspopup` describes a popup that opens
  when an element is activated, and a right-click on a row isn't that. So nothing tells a screen
  reader user the menu is there, and on macOS only VoiceOver opens it from the keyboard: every action
  in it has to be reachable from a visible control as well, which
  [WCAG 2.1.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html) asks for.

And around it:

- The menu isn't modal. A press outside it closes it and does whatever it does, the rest of the page
  stays reachable, and nothing locks scrolling.
- Nothing listens on the page while the menu is closed, so a table with a menu on every row adds no
  listeners until one opens.
- The menu doesn't animate.
summary: The `ContextMenu` component opens a menu of actions where you right-click an element, such as a table row or a card, or long press it on a touch screen. Shift+F10 and the context menu key open it too, where the browser fires `contextmenu` for them, which Windows and Linux do. The menu is Dropdown's markup, portaled into the `portalContainer` a `ConfigProvider` sets, or the end of the trigger's own document's `<body>`, so it never has server markup. It opens below and to the right of the point, flips above or to the left where there's no room, moves in where it fits neither way, and scrolls inside when it's taller than the viewport. It doesn't follow the trigger, since scrolling closes it. Inside a `Modal` or a shadow root, point `portalContainer` inside it, so screen readers that honor `aria-modal` reach the menu and the shadow root's styles apply. Opening moves focus to the first enabled item. The arrow keys, Home, End and typing move between items, and Enter and Space activate one. Escape, Tab, an item, a press outside, scrolling, resizing and the window losing focus close it, handing focus back to what had it unless an item moved it somewhere else. For a menu opened from a button use `Dropdown`.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element a right-click, Shift+F10, the context menu key or a long press opens the menu from: a table row, a card, an image. It's cloned, not wrapped, so a row stays a row, which means it has to be a single element that passes `className` and the `onContextMenu`, `onPointerDown`, `onPointerMove`, `onPointerUp`, `onPointerCancel` and `onTouchEnd` handlers to its DOM node. Its own handlers for those run first, and one that calls `preventDefault()` on `contextmenu` keeps the menu closed. A `ContextMenu` inside it opens instead of this one. It gets no ARIA and no tab stop, since it can be any element and a right-click isn't an activation. Keyboard users reach it through something focusable inside it, such as the row's own `Dropdown` button, or a `tabIndex={0}` you give it, and press Shift+F10 or the context menu key there. It gets `-webkit-touch-callout: none`, so iOS doesn't put its own callout for a link or an image over the menu. A long press still selects text the way it does anywhere, so give a region where it shouldn't `interaction="unselectable"`.

props.name: children
props.description: The menu's items: `ContextMenu.Item` and `ContextMenu.Divider`, the same components as `Dropdown.Item` and `Dropdown.Divider`. Every action in it needs a visible way in as well, such as a `Dropdown` on the same row: nothing tells a screen reader user the menu is there, and on macOS only VoiceOver opens it from the keyboard.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with `true` when the menu opens and `false` when it closes, whatever closed it, such as for highlighting the row whose menu is open. Nothing fires after ContextMenu unmounts. There's no `open` prop to go with it: a menu opened from code has no point to open at.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu when an item is clicked, or activated with Enter or Space. A click on a divider or between items leaves it open either way.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Leave the trigger to the browser: a right-click shows the browser's own menu, a long press does what it does anywhere, and an open menu closes.

extraProps.name: aria-label
extraProps.description: The menu's accessible name, such as "Actions for report.pdf". There's no button to borrow a name from, so pass this or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build warns when the menu opens with neither.

extraProps.name: className
extraProps.description: Additional classes for the menu (`role="menu"`). The trigger keeps its own.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

props.name: as
props.description: The element type to render. `'button'` renders `type="button"` unless you pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"`, so an item inside a form does not submit it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Marks the item as disabled; disabled items are skipped during keyboard navigation. Use with `as="button"` for a native disabled control, or pair with `aria-disabled` on a link.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element selected by as and Bulma helper props
